name: Deadlift
pattern: Hip hinge: a weight is lifted from the floor (or from a hang) by driving the hips forward while the spine stays still.
setup: Feet hip width, the bar over the middle of your feet, close to your shins.
Push your hips back and bend your knees until your hands reach the bar just outside your legs.
Chest up, back flat, shoulders over or just in front of the bar.
Pull the slack out of the bar: arms long, armpits squeezed, brace your belly.

steps.text: Brace, flat back, bar against your shins.
Push the floor away. Hips and shoulders rise together, the bar slides up your legs.
Stand tall: squeeze your glutes until your hips are straight. Do not lean back.
Hips back first, then bend the knees once the bar passes them. Keep the bar close.

cues.cue: Flat back from setup to lockout.
cues.why: Spine loads in a heavy pull are very high; a neutral spine keeps them on the strongest posture.

cues.cue: Bar over midfoot and touching your legs the whole way.
cues.why: Where the bar starts changes knee, hip and torso angles and which muscles work.

cues.cue: Hips and shoulders rise at the same speed.
cues.why: Hips that shoot up first turn the lift into a stiff-leg pull and put the load on the back.

cues.cue: Push the floor away, then drive the hips through.
cues.why: The quads work most early in the lift; glutes and back extensors finish it.

cues.cue: Finish with glutes, ribs down. Stand straight, not backwards.
cues.why: Leaning back at the top adds spine extension load without more hip work.

breathing: Big breath and brace before each pull; breathe out at the top or after the bar is back down.

tempo.note: Lift with intent, lower under control, reset your brace on the floor.

mistakes.name: Rounded back
mistakes.looks: The lower back curves like a cat as the bar leaves the floor.
mistakes.fix: Lower the weight, chest up, brace harder, start with the bar closer.
mistakes.why: A flexed spine under a heavy load is a weaker and riskier posture.

mistakes.name: Hips shoot up
mistakes.looks: The hips rise before the bar moves; the legs straighten and the chest drops.
mistakes.fix: Push with the legs first; keep the chest angle until the bar passes the knees.
mistakes.why: The back ends up doing the lift the legs should start.

mistakes.name: Bar drifts forward
mistakes.looks: The bar swings away from the legs in front of the toes.
mistakes.fix: Squeeze your armpits and drag the bar up your legs.
mistakes.why: A bar farther forward lengthens the lever on the hips and lower back.

mistakes.name: Leaning back at lockout
mistakes.looks: At the top the hips push forward and the shoulders fall behind the heels.
mistakes.fix: Stop when you are standing straight; squeeze glutes, ribs down.
mistakes.why: Extra arch at the top loads the lumbar joints without adding hip work.

safety: Low back pain: start with trap bar or blocks to shorten the range; stop if pain travels down the leg.
Keep the load where you can hold a flat back; form breaks first near failure.
Use chalk or straps before a mixed grip for heavy sets; a mixed grip twists the shoulders.

variants.change: Wide stance (about twice hip width), toes out about 40°, hands inside the knees: trunk 5-10° more upright, less bar travel, more quads.
Handles at your sides: more knee bend, more knee work, lower hip and back moments; most people lift more.
Starts standing, knees soft and fixed; lower only as far as the hips go back with a flat back.
Knees almost straight from the floor: most hamstring stretch; use lighter loads.
Standing on a plate: more range at the bottom, more knee and hip bend at setup.
Bar starts at or below the knee: shorter range, heavier loads, less leg drive.
Stop 1-2 s just off the floor or below the knee while holding position.
Load grows toward the top; the lockout gets harder.
Weight in one hand at your side: the trunk must resist leaning to that side.
Back foot on its toes for balance; most of the load on the front leg.
Weights hang between or beside the legs; same hinge, lighter load.

subtypes.name: Sumo deadlift
subtypes.change: Wide stance, toes out, more upright trunk, hands inside knees. Jefferson is an asymmetric straddle version.

subtypes.name: Romanian / stiff-leg deadlift
subtypes.change: Starts at the top, knees soft and fixed, hips travel back until the bar is near mid-shin.

subtypes.name: Trap bar deadlift
subtypes.change: Handles at the sides: more knee bend, more upright trunk.

subtypes.name: Rack pull / block pull
subtypes.change: Bar starts at the knee; only the top half of the lift.

subtypes.name: Cable pull-through
subtypes.change: Facing away from a low cable, rope between the legs; hinge back, then drive the hips forward. Load pulls backward, not down.

metrics.label: Trunk angle change before the bar passes the knee

motion.basis: Relative angles from escamilla2000 (sumo trunk 5-10° more upright, thigh 11-16° more horizontal, conventional knees and hips about 12° more extended at lift-off, stance 70 vs 32 cm, toes out 42 vs 14°) and swinton2011 (trap bar more knee, less hip and back moment). Absolute joint angles are estimates built from those differences and the bar-over-midfoot geometry; trunk = hipFlex - thigh angle from vertical. Arms hang vertically, so shoulderFlex is about the trunk angle minus 5.
